mainTopic: A בעל קרי and דאורייתא versus דרבנן; Torah sources for ברכות; doubts about שמע and תפלה; davening a second time
overview: The amud opens by asking why a בעל קרי thinks the words of קריאת שמע and says ברכת המזון, but may not begin תפלה. After an answer about מלכות שמים is rejected, the גמרא concludes that שמע and ברכת המזון are דאורייתא while תפלה is דרבנן. רב יהודה then brings פסוקים showing that ברכת המזון after eating and ברכת התורה before learning are from the Torah. רבי יוחנן tries to derive the other two ברכות from these by קל וחומר, but his statement is refuted. Next, רב יהודה rules that a doubt about שמע is not repeated, while a doubt about אמת ויציב is, because he holds שמע is דרבנן. The גמרא defends him against challenges from a פסוק and from the משנה. רבי אלעזר disagrees about שמע, and רבי יוחנן says one who is unsure should daven again. The amud ends with שמואל's rulings about someone who already davened, and begins explaining why both rulings are needed.

steps.title: תפלה is also communal, yet he may not begin it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's reason using תפלה: the community is busy with it too, yet a בעל קרי who has not started may not start.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about תפלה? It is also something the community is busy with. And we learned in a משנה: if someone was standing in תפלה and remembered he is a בעל קרי, he should not stop, but should shorten it. The reason he continues is only because he already started. If he had not started, he should not start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason just given for why a בעל קרי thinks the words of שמע: 'because everyone else is doing it.' It points out that this reason should also apply to תפלה, but it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'the community is busy with it' were enough, a בעל קרי should be allowed to begin תפלה too. But the משנה only lets him continue a תפלה he already started, which shows he may not begin one. So 'the community is busy with it' cannot be the full reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at... (opens a challenge from another case)
Something the community is busy with
A man who had a seminal emission and has not yet gone to the מקוה
The reason is because...; but if not... (drawing an inference from what the משנה says)

phrases.english: But what about prayer,
which is something the community is busy with,
and we learned: if he was standing in prayer
and remembered that he is a בעל קרי,
he should not stop, but should shorten it.
The reason is that he already began,
but if he did not begin, he should not begin!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי תְּפִלָּה, דְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר עֲסוּקִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's reason from before this section, that a בעל קרי thinks the words of שמע because the community is busy with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reason: 'so he will not sit idle while the community is busy'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפלה is also communal, yet the משנה implies a בעל קרי may not begin it. So the communal reason does not hold up on its own.

steps.title: תפלה has no מלכות שמים
steps.stepSummary: First answer: תפלה is different because it does not contain קבלת עול מלכות שמים, the way שמע does.
steps.simpleTranslation: תפלה is different, because it does not have מלכות שמים in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying שמע has something special that תפלה lacks: accepting God as King.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the communal reason applies only to something that includes מלכות שמים, like שמע. Since תפלה lacks it, a בעל קרי does not need to join in. This answer is about to be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingdom of Heaven, meaning accepting God as King, as in שמע

phrases.english: Prayer is different,
since it does not contain the kingdom of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי תְּפִלָּה דְּלֵית בַּהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by pointing to a difference between תפלה and שמע.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenger thought anything communal should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only something with מלכות שמים, like שמע, is said in his heart. תפלה lacks this, so he does not begin it.

steps.title: ברכת המזון also lacks מלכות שמים, yet he says it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the first answer: ברכת המזון also has no מלכות שמים, yet the משנה says a בעל קרי says the blessing after eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ברכת המזון after eating has no מלכות שמים in it either. And we learned in the משנה: over food, he says the blessing after it, but does not say the blessing before it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer from step 2 by bringing a case that breaks the pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If missing מלכות שמים were the reason a בעל קרי skips something, he should also skip ברכת המזון. But the משנה says he does say ברכת המזון after eating. So the lack of מלכות שמים cannot be the real difference.

phrases.english: But what about the blessing after the meal,
which does not contain the kingdom of Heaven,
and we learned: over food he blesses afterward,
phrases.notes: This is from our own משנה, which lists what a בעל קרי still says.

phrases.english: but does not bless beforehand!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן לְאַחֲרָיו דְּלֵית בַּהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 2 with a case that does not fit it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the distinction based on מלכות שמים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ברכת המזון also lacks מלכות שמים, yet a בעל קרי does say it, so that cannot be what decides the matter.

steps.title: Torah-level obligations versus a Rabbinic one
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: קריאת שמע and ברכת המזון are מדאורייתא, while תפלה is מדרבנן. That is why he says the first two in his heart but does not begin תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the real difference is this: קריאת שמע and ברכת המזון are from the Torah, and תפלה is from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier answer and gives a new one. The dividing line is whether the מצוה comes from the Torah or from the Rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because שמע and ברכת המזון are Torah obligations, a בעל קרי still fulfills them, at least in his heart. תפלה is only rabbinic, so the Rabbis did not require him to begin it while impure. This explains every case: שמע, ברכת המזון, and תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: A בעל קרי says (in his heart) the Torah-level מצוות of שמע and ברכת המזון, but does not begin the rabbinic מצוה of תפלה.
steps.confusionAlert: The final answer is not 'what the community does' and not 'מלכות שמים.' Both of those were tested and set aside. The real line is דאורייתא versus דרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question that follows: where in the Torah do we see that ברכת המזון is דאורייתא? רב יהודה answers that next.

phrases.english: Rather: the reading of שמע
and the blessing after meals are from the Torah,
and prayer is from the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 2 with a new difference that fits all the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the difference might be the presence of מלכות שמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah-level obligations, like שמע and ברכת המזון, are said in his heart. The rabbinic obligation of תפלה is not begun.

steps.title: Torah source for ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה brings the פסוק that shows ברכת המזון after eating is a Torah obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Where do we see that the blessing after the meal is from the Torah? Because it says: 'And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless.'
steps.whatsHappening: Right after saying ברכת המזון is דאורייתא, the גמרא brings רב יהודה's source for that from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the blessing after eating and being full, so the Torah obligation is the blessing after the meal. This backs up the answer in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall eat, be satisfied, and bless

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
From where do we know the blessing after the meal
is from the Torah?
As it says: 'And you shall eat and be satisfied and bless.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מִנַּיִן לְבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן לְאַחֲרֶיהָ מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for the claim in step 4 that ברכת המזון is דאורייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת המזון after eating is a Torah obligation, learned from 'ואכלת ושבעת וברכת.'

steps.title: Torah source for ברכת התורה before learning
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה continues: the ברכת התורה before learning is also from the Torah, learned from a פסוק in שירת האזינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that the blessing before the Torah is from the Torah? Because it says: 'When I call out the name of ה׳, give greatness to our God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה adds a second Torah-level blessing: the blessing said before learning or reading Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read this way: before I 'call out ה׳'s name' by reading Torah, give praise to God by making a blessing. Notice the timing: ברכת המזון is after the meal, while ברכת התורה is before the learning.
steps.whatToRemember: Two Torah-level blessings: ברכת המזון after eating (from ואכלת ושבעת וברכת) and ברכת התורה before learning (from כי שם ה׳ אקרא).

phrases.english: From where do we know the blessing before the Torah
is from the Torah?
As it says: 'When I call out the name of the Lord,'
give greatness to our God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְבִרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה לְפָנֶיהָ מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's teaching with a second Torah-level blessing, parallel to step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת התורה before learning is a Torah obligation, learned from 'כי שם ה׳ אקרא הבו גדל לאלהינו.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Two blessings learned from each other
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ברכה after Torah is learned from ברכת המזון, and the ברכה before food is learned from ברכת התורה, each by a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We learned the blessing after the Torah from the blessing over food by a קל וחומר, and the blessing before food from the blessing over the Torah by a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes a short headline claim about two ברכות. The next two steps will spell out each argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last steps showed that the ברכה after food and the ברכה before Torah are from the Torah. רבי יוחנן now uses each one to fill the gap in the other: Torah gets a ברכה after, and food gets a ברכה before.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if a weaker case has a rule, a stronger case surely has it too
The blessing said over learning Torah

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
We learned the blessing over the Torah after it
from the blessing over food, through a קל וחומר,
and the blessing over food before it
from the blessing over the Torah, through a קל וחומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָמַדְנוּ בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה לְאַחֲרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב יהודה's two Torah sources, the ברכה after food and the ברכה before Torah, to derive the missing ברכה for each.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה after Torah and the ברכה before food are each derived by קל וחומר from the other.

steps.title: First argument: a blessing after Torah
steps.stepSummary: Food needs no ברכה before it but needs one after. Torah needs one before, so it surely needs one after.
steps.simpleTranslation: The blessing after the Torah from the blessing over food by a קל וחומר: If food, which does not need a blessing before it, needs one after it, then Torah, which does need one before it, surely needs one after it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן spells out the first קל וחומר, showing why Torah should need a ברכה afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food looks like the 'weaker' case because it has no Torah-level ברכה before it, yet it still has a ברכה after. Torah is 'stronger' because it already has a ברכה before. So it should surely have one after too.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? (the closing words of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: The blessing over the Torah after it
from the blessing over food, through a קל וחומר:
If food, which does not require a blessing before it,
phrases.notes: He means not required by the Torah. The פסוק from Step 5 only speaks about a ברכה after eating.

phrases.english: requires one after it,
then Torah, which does require one before it,
isn't it logical that it requires one after it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of רבי יוחנן's claim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah needs a ברכה afterward, by קל וחומר from food.

steps.title: Second argument: a blessing before food
steps.stepSummary: Torah needs no ברכה after it but needs one before. Food needs one after, so it surely needs one before.
steps.simpleTranslation: The blessing before food from the blessing over the Torah by a קל וחומר: If Torah, which does not need a blessing after it, needs one before it, then food, which does need one after it, surely needs one before it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן spells out the second קל וחומר, which runs the same logic in the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now Torah is the 'weaker' case, since it has a Torah-level ברכה only before it. Food is 'stronger' because it already has a ברכה after. So food should surely have a ברכה before too.

phrases.english: And the blessing over food before it
from the blessing over the Torah, through a קל וחומר:
If Torah, which does not require a blessing after it,
requires one before it,
then food, which does require one after it,
isn't it logical that it should require one before it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second half of רבי יוחנן's claim, as the mirror image of Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food needs a ברכה beforehand, by קל וחומר from Torah.

steps.title: Both arguments can be broken
steps.stepSummary: Food is special because a person enjoys it, and Torah is special because it is eternal life. So neither can teach the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: One can refute this: Food is different, because one gets pleasure from it. And Torah is different, because it is eternal life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא breaks both קל וחומר arguments by showing that each source has something special that the other does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is truly 'weaker' in every way. Food has a ברכה after because we enjoy it, and Torah has none of that bodily pleasure. Torah has a ברכה before because it gives eternal life, and food does not. So each ברכה may come from a reason unique to its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: One can refute it (break the logic)

phrases.english: One can refute this:
What about food? It is special, since one gets pleasure from it.
And what about Torah? It is special, since it is eternal life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks both קל וחומר arguments from Steps 8 and 9.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each source case has a unique feature (pleasure for food, eternal life for Torah), so it is not truly 'weaker' than the case being learned.

steps.title: The משנה says no blessing before food
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says a בעל קרי blesses after food but not before it. That suggests the ברכה before food is not from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, we learned in the משנה: Over food, he blesses after it but does not bless before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a stronger attack: a משנה goes against רבי יוחנן's second argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets a בעל קרי say ברכת המזון afterward because it is from the Torah. It does not let him say the ברכה before eating. If רבי יוחנן's קל וחומר made the ברכה before food a Torah obligation, the משנה would allow that too.

phrases.english: And furthermore, we learned in the משנה:
Over food, he blesses after it,
phrases.notes: This is our משנה about a בעל קרי, the same one mentioned in Step 3.

phrases.english: but does not bless before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a source-based attack on top of the logical refutation in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the ברכה before food is a Torah-level obligation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats the ברכה before food differently from the ברכה after food, so it does not see the ברכה before as from the Torah.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's statement is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן's statement is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its verdict: רבי יוחנן's teaching is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With both the logical break and the משנה against it, רבי יוחנן's statement does not stand. A תיובתא means the view is rejected, not just questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה after Torah and the ברכה before food cannot be learned from each other by קל וחומר, and רבי יוחנן's statement is refuted.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the attack from Steps 10 and 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's two קל וחומר arguments are rejected.

steps.title: Unsure whether he said שמע or אמת ויציב
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules: if unsure about קריאת שמע, don't repeat it. If unsure about אמת ויציב, repeat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: If he is unsure whether he read קריאת שמע or not, he does not go back and read it. If he is unsure whether he said 'אמת ויציב' or not, he goes back and says 'אמת ויציב'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רב יהודה gives two rulings about a person who is in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprise is that the main part, שמע, is not repeated, while the ברכה after it is repeated. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה right after שמע in the morning

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
If he is unsure whether he read קריאת שמע
or did not read it,
he does not go back and read it.
If he is unsure whether he said 'אמת ויציב'
or did not say it,
he goes back and says 'אמת ויציב'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: סָפֵק קָרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that is still tied to whether a מצוה is דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In doubt, שמע is not repeated, but אמת ויציב is repeated.

steps.title: Why the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב יהודה's two rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the two cases are treated differently. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems backwards to be stricter about the ברכה than about שמע itself. The question asks what principle explains this.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אמת ויציב is repeated in a doubt but שמע is not

steps.title: שמע is דרבנן, אמת ויציב is דאורייתא
steps.stepSummary: According to רב יהודה, קריאת שמע is only דרבנן, while אמת ויציב is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: קריאת שמע is from the Rabbis. 'אמת ויציב' is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רב יהודה holds that שמע is a rabbinic מצוה and אמת ויציב is a Torah מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there is a doubt about a rabbinic מצוה we are lenient, so he does not repeat שמע. When there is a doubt about a Torah מצוה we are strict, so he repeats אמת ויציב. אמת ויציב is from the Torah because it fulfills remembering יציאת מצרים.
steps.confusionAlert: In Step 4 the גמרא said קריאת שמע is מדאורייתא. רב יהודה here holds a different view, that שמע is only דרבנן. That is exactly why רב יוסף challenges him next.

phrases.english: קריאת שמע is from the Rabbis.
'אמת ויציב' is from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמע is דרבנן, so a doubt is treated leniently. אמת ויציב is דאורייתא, so a doubt is treated strictly.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The פסוק says 'when you lie down and when you rise'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects: the Torah clearly says 'ובשכבך ובקומך', so how can שמע be only דרבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: 'And when you lie down and when you rise.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges the idea that שמע is דרבנן by quoting a פסוק that seems to command it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ובשכבך ובקומך' appear in the פרשה of שמע and sound like a command to say it at night and in the morning. If so, שמע is from the Torah, and a doubt should be treated strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (usually from a source)
When you lie down and when you rise

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raises an objection:
'And when you lie down and when you rise.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in Step 15 that שמע is דרבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קריאת שמע is only דרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק seems to directly command saying שמע at night and in the morning, which would make it דאורייתא.

steps.title: אביי: That פסוק is about learning Torah
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that 'ובשכבך ובקומך' is written about learning Torah in general, not about saying שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: That פסוק is written about words of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב יהודה by reading the פסוק in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ודברת בם', speak about them, which can mean learning Torah at all times, even when lying down and getting up. Read that way, it is not a command to say the פרשה of שמע. So שמע can still be דרבנן according to רב יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה holds that שמע is דרבנן, so a doubt is not repeated, while אמת ויציב is דאורייתא and is repeated. אביי explains that 'ובשכבך ובקומך' is about learning Torah.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
That פסוק is written about words of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הָהוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection from Step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק commands saying שמע, so שמע would be דאורייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is about general Torah learning, so שמע can be דרבנן in רב יהודה's view.

steps.title: Citing the משנה about a בעל קרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה: a בעל קרי thinks שמע in his heart and says no ברכות before or after it, but after eating he does say ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: a בעל קרי thinks the words of שמע in his heart, and he does not say the ברכות before it or after it. But for food, he says the ברכה after eating, and not the one before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to set up a test of רב יהודה's claim that אמת ויציב is דאורייתא. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats two kinds of ברכות differently for a בעל קרי. He skips the ברכה after שמע, but he says the ברכה after food, which the Torah requires. This contrast is the raw material for the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had a seminal emission and has not yet gone to the מקוה
Thinks it in his heart, without saying the words out loud

phrases.english: We learned: one who had a seminal emission thinks [שמע] in his heart
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from the previous page. Thinking it in his heart means not saying the words out loud.

phrases.english: and does not recite a blessing, neither before it
nor after it.
And over food, he recites a blessing after it
but does not recite a blessing before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the argument about whether שמע is דאורייתא to testing whether אמת ויציב is דאורייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether אמת ויציב is דאורייתא, as רב יהודה claimed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a בעל קרי (ברכות פרק ג)

steps.title: If it were from the Torah, he should say it
steps.stepSummary: If אמת ויציב were דאורייתא, the בעל קרי should say it, just like he says ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that אמת ויציב is from the Torah, then he should say the ברכה after שמע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the משנה to challenge רב יהודה. The בעל קרי says ברכת המזון because it is from the Torah, so if אמת ויציב were from the Torah, he should say it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows the rule: a בעל קרי still says ברכות that are דאורייתא, like ברכת המזון. Since he does not say the ברכה after שמע, it looks like אמת ויציב is only דרבנן. That goes against step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
The ברכה said right after שמע in the morning

phrases.english: And if it would enter your mind
that 'אמת ויציב' is from the Torah,
let him recite the blessing after it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim (step 15) that אמת ויציב is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בעל קרי says Torah-level ברכות (like ברכת המזון). He skips the ברכה after שמע, so it must not be Torah-level.

steps.title: He already mentioned leaving Egypt in שמע
steps.stepSummary: The Torah part of אמת ויציב is remembering יציאת מצרים, and the בעל קרי already did that through שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does a person say אמת ויציב? If it is because of יציאת מצרים, he already mentioned that in קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It explains that the בעל קרי does not need אמת ויציב, because its Torah purpose was already covered by שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah reason for אמת ויציב is to remember יציאת מצרים. The last part of שמע (the פרשה of ציצית) already mentions יציאת מצרים. So the בעל קרי skipping אמת ויציב does not prove it is only דרבנן; he simply already did his Torah duty.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying אמת ויציב is דרבנן. It is saying the בעל קרי already did its Torah job inside שמע, so the משנה proves nothing.

phrases.english: What is the reason he recites [this] blessing?
If it is because of the going out of Egypt,
he has already mentioned it in the reading of שמע.
phrases.notes: The last paragraph of שמע, about ציצית, ends by mentioning leaving Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה that אמת ויציב is only דרבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The בעל קרי skips אמת ויציב because its Torah purpose (remembering יציאת מצרים) was already done through שמע, not because it is דרבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining away the inference: the Torah purpose of אמת ויציב was already done through שמע
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the בעל קרי skips the ברכה after שמע, אמת ויציב must be only דרבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בעל קרי skips אמת ויציב because he already mentioned יציאת מצרים in שמע. So אמת ויציב can still be דאורייתא, as רב יהודה said.

steps.title: Why not say אמת ויציב instead of שמע?
steps.stepSummary: If both mention יציאת מצרים, let him say אמת ויציב and skip שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him say this one (אמת ויציב) and not need that one (שמע)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. If either one can cover יציאת מצרים, why must the בעל קרי use שמע rather than אמת ויציב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said שמע covers the מצוה of remembering יציאת מצרים. But אמת ויציב covers it just as well. So why does the משנה have him think שמע and skip אמת ויציב, and not the other way around?

keyTerms.meaning: And let him say this one
and he will not need that one

phrases.english: So let him say this, and he will not need that!
phrases.notes: 'This' is אמת ויציב, and 'that' is שמע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 20 that שמע covers the remembering of יציאת מצרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both texts remember יציאת מצרים equally, there is no reason to choose שמע over אמת ויציב.

steps.title: שמע is better because it has two things
steps.stepSummary: שמע is preferred because it contains two things, and אמת ויציב contains only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: קריאת שמע is better, because it has two things in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמע is chosen because it does more than אמת ויציב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמע has both remembering יציאת מצרים and accepting עול מלכות שמים. אמת ויציב only has the first. So when only one can be done, שמע wins, and the answer of step 20 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: A בעל קרי skipping אמת ויציב does not prove it is דרבנן. He covers יציאת מצרים through שמע, which is better because it has two things in it.

phrases.english: The reading of שמע is preferable,
because it has two [things] in it.
phrases.notes: The two things are remembering leaving Egypt and accepting עול מלכות שמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranking: one text is preferred because it contains more content
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמע and אמת ויציב are equal for remembering יציאת מצרים, so either could be chosen.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמע is preferred because it also has קבלת עול מלכות שמים, so the defense of רב יהודה from step 20 stands.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר on doubts about שמע and תפילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a doubt about קריאת שמע means you say it again, but a doubt about תפילה does not mean you daven again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: if someone is not sure whether he said קריאת שמע, he goes back and says it. If he is not sure whether he davened, he does not go back and daven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אלעזר that treats a doubt about שמע differently from a doubt about davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ורבי אלעזר אמר' mark a disagreement with רב יהודה from step 13, who ruled that a doubt about שמע is not repeated. רבי אלעזר says the opposite: a doubt about שמע is repeated, but a doubt about תפילה is not. The usual explanation is that he holds שמע is a Torah obligation, while תפילה is a rabbinic one, and with a doubt about a rabbinic obligation we are lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt; not sure whether something happened
Davened, meaning he said שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
If he is unsure whether he recited the Shema
or did not recite it,
he goes back and recites the Shema.
If he is unsure whether he prayed or did not pray,
he does not go back and pray.
phrases.notes: Here 'pray' means the עמידה, the silent שמונה עשרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב יהודה's ruling in step 13 and disagrees with it: רבי אלעזר holds that a doubt about שמע is repeated. He adds that a doubt about תפילה is not repeated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubt about קריאת שמע requires saying it again. A doubt about תפילה does not require davening again.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: if only a person would daven all day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees about the doubt in תפילה and says a person should daven again, because davening more is a good thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: if only a person would daven the whole day long!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן responds to the second half of רבי אלעזר's ruling and argues that someone unsure whether he davened should daven again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said there is no need to daven again when in doubt. רבי יוחנן turns that around: davening is so valuable that extra davening is welcome. So when in doubt, there is no reason to hold back.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If only a person would pray
phrases.notes: He is answering רבי אלעזר: if you are unsure whether you davened, go ahead and daven again.

phrases.english: the entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: וּלְוַאי שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of רבי אלעזר's ruling, about a doubt in תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone unsure whether he davened should daven again, because extra davening is desirable.

steps.title: Stop at once if you realize you already davened
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that someone who remembers in the middle of שמונה עשרה that he already davened must stop, even in the middle of a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if someone was standing in תפילה and remembered that he had already davened, he stops, even in the middle of a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: a person who realizes he is repeating a תפילה he already said must stop right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he already davened, this second תפילה is not needed. So he does not even finish the ברכה he is in. He stops right where he is.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing in the middle of שמונה עשרה
In the middle of a ברכה

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If one was standing in prayer
and remembered that he had already prayed, he stops,
even in the middle of a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about davening, related in topic to the previous discussion of extra תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who realizes mid-תפילה that he already davened stops immediately, even in the middle of a ברכה.

steps.title: Challenge: on שבת a mistaken weekday ברכה is finished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from רבה בר אבוה's ruling that someone who mistakenly started a weekday ברכה on שבת finishes that ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't רב נחמן say: when we were at רבה בר אבוה's place, we asked him: these students who make a mistake and start saying the weekday ברכות on שבת, should they finish? And he told us: they finish that whole ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions שמואל's ruling by bringing a case where someone who started an unneeded ברכה by mistake does finish it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת the weekday middle ברכות are not said. Still, רבה בר אבוה ruled that someone who started one by mistake completes it. That seems to contradict שמואל, who said a person who realizes his mistake stops even in the middle of a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A word that opens a challenge
Of the weekday, meaning a weekday ברכה of שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Rav Naḥman say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: When we were at the house of Rabba bar Avuh,
we asked him:
These students of the yeshiva
who mistakenly mention a weekday blessing on Shabbat,
what is the law, should they finish?
And he said to us:
They finish that entire blessing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's ruling from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that one stops even in the middle of a ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In another case of a mistaken, unneeded ברכה (a weekday ברכה on שבת), the ruling is to finish the ברכה, so the same should apply here.

steps.title: The cases are different: on שבת he really is obligated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that on שבת the person is really obligated in a full תפילה, and the רבנן only spared him, but here he already davened.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, the person is really obligated in those ברכות, and it is only the רבנן who did not burden him because of כבוד שבת. But here, he already davened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the comparison and explains why someone who started a weekday ברכה on שבת is different from someone who already davened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת the weekday ברכות are basically fitting for him. The רבנן left them out only so as not to burden him on שבת, so once he started one, he finishes it. In שמואל's case he already completed his obligation, so the extra תפילה has no place at all, and he stops immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? The cases are not alike

steps.whatToRemember: Finishing a ברכה started by mistake depends on whether the person really belongs to that תפילה. On שבת he does, and the רבנן only spared him the burden, so he finishes. Someone who already davened has no place in the extra תפילה, so he stops right away.

phrases.english: How can you compare!
There, the man is someone who is obligated,
phrases.notes: He means that in principle he is obligated in all the regular ברכות, even on שבת.

phrases.english: and it is the Sages who did not burden him
because of the honor of Shabbat,
but here, he has already prayed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא! הָתָם גַּבְרָא בַּר חִיּוּבָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by showing that the two cases are not alike.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any mistaken, unneeded ברכה should be treated the same, so it should be finished.
steps.terutzMaskana: On שבת the person is basically obligated and was only spared by the רבנן, so he finishes. Someone who already davened has no obligation at all, so he stops.

steps.title: Davening again with a צבור only if you add something new
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that someone who already davened and finds a צבור davening may daven again only if he can add something new to his תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if someone already davened, then went into a בית הכנסת and found the צבור davening, if he can add something new to it, he may daven again. If not, he should not daven again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of שמואל about davening a second time, this time when joining a צבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This balances the earlier rulings. A second תפילה is not automatically allowed, but it is not completely forbidden either. It is allowed when he adds something new to it, so that it is not just a repeat of what he already said.

keyTerms.meaning: To add something new to the תפילה

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If one prayed and then entered a synagogue
and found a congregation that is praying,
if he can add something new to it,
he may pray again,
and if not, he should not pray again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הִתְפַּלֵּל וְנִכְנַס לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling of שמואל about a second תפילה, this time in the setting of a צבור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who already davened may daven again with a צבור only if he adds something new; otherwise he may not.

steps.title: Why both of שמואל's rulings are needed: the first case alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a צריכותא, explaining that both of שמואל's rulings are needed. If we only had the first one, we might think it applies only to an individual davening alone both times.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both statements are needed. If שמואל had only taught us the first one, we would have said that it applies only to an individual who davened and then davened again as an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל needed to say two rulings that look alike. This line only gives the first half of the reasoning; the גמרא is setting up the next move, which will explain what the second ruling adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rulings seem to teach the same idea: once you davened, you don't just daven again. The גמרא says the first ruling (stop in the middle, step 25) by itself would only cover an individual repeating his own תפילה alone. That leaves open the case of someone who finds a צבור davening, which the second ruling (step 28) will address.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary: the opening word of a צריכותא, explaining why two similar teachings are both needed
These words apply (only) to…; this limits a rule to a certain case
An individual davening alone, not with a צבור

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. The גמרא is only explaining why שמואל said two rulings that sound like the same idea, and this line is only the first half of that explanation.

phrases.english: And it is necessary (to have both statements),
phrases.notes: He means both of שמואל's rulings: stopping in the middle (step 25) and davening again with a צבור (step 28).

phrases.english: for if he had taught us only the first one,
(we would say) that applies only to an individual and an individual
phrases.notes: He davened alone the first time and was davening alone again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After quoting שמואל's second ruling (step 28), the גמרא explains why it was needed alongside the first ruling (step 25), starting with what the first ruling alone would cover.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first ruling alone might be limited to an individual davening alone both times, so another ruling is needed for other cases.
